question: For Plasmodium falciparum malaria in children, Artemisinin Combination Therapy (ACT) is the first-line treatment, while for Plasmodium vivax, the standard regimen is chloroquine plus primaquine after checking G6PD status.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is TRUE. Falciparum malaria treatment = ACT (not chloroquine, which has widespread falciparum resistance). Vivax malaria = chloroquine + primaquine (to eliminate hypnozoites and prevent relapse). Before prescribing primaquine, always screen for G6PD deficiency — primaquine causes life-threatening haemolysis in G6PD-deficient children.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. NVBDCP guidelines: P. falciparum → ACT (artemether-lumefantrine or artesunate-based combination). P. vivax → chloroquine for blood-stage clearance + primaquine (14-day course) to eliminate liver hypnozoites and prevent relapse. ALWAYS check G6PD status before primaquine — G6PD deficiency causes severe haemolysis with primaquine.
